newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHARES EASE, SEEN FLAT OR SLIGHTLY DOWN.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHARES EASE, SEEN FLAT OR SLIGHTLY DOWN.

text.p: Polish shares eased after a three-session slight gain and analysts said the market would likely maintain its general flat trend in the mid-term as large upcoming public offerings countered good macroeconomic data.

"Even though inflation is going well, even though we have large public offerings coming, I don't expect the inflation news to cause bourse rises, nor the primary offer serious falls," said Roman Sosnowski of Bank Staropolski brokerage.
Analysts said Tuesday's stronger selling after price fixing could signal another dip on Wednesday, which could be deepened should the U.S. raise interest rates later on Tuesday.

"If interest rates there rise that could be a signal for bourses prices to fall even here," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski of Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage, adding that speculative domestic investors might do most of the selling.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.1 percent to 16,453.3 points and turnover was flat at 133.1 million zlotys on all three markets.

The public offering of Bank Handlowy, which starts in late May and is expected to draw cash from listed stocks, is seen worth about $1 billion. Analysts also said the overall market seemed fairly valued at current levels.
Analysts said Tuesday's biggest loser, Prochnik , fell 8.9 percent in light trade in reaction to its recent rise and April net loss reported on Monday.

They said banks' recent rebound from deep falls was seen short-lived as the sector's earnings this year would likely remain sub-par after central bank decisions this year to increase reserve requirements.
Large-cap WBK rose 2.8 percent in moderate trade in the regular session but the sector was mixed in continuous trade, where the WIG 20 index fell 1.2 percent.
